findings.highlight: My fever's so hot, it'd burn anyone who touched me. It feels like my brain is melting and oozing right out of my skull.
findings.evidenceJa: 人を黒こげにするほどの熱病にでもかかったのか、頭の中はとっくに溶けて、耳から流れ出したかのよう。
findings.governingReading: He feels as though afflicted by heat that could char a person, with an already-melted head draining through the ears.
findings.explanation: An as-if charring fever gains a contact-burn threat to others.

findings.highlight: Somehow, in spite of it all, I still cling to consciousness. Pain is an old friend. I know how to endure it.
findings.evidenceJa: ……意識は保てる。自分だけの痛みなら、自分だけが耐えればいいだけ。そんな事なら、問題はない。
findings.governingReading: If pain is his alone, only he needs to endure it, so that poses no problem.
findings.explanation: Only his own pain being bearable becomes Pain is an old friend.

findings.highlight: "A champion of justice is someone who can only clean up a mess that's already been made. You'll never be able to save the very people you're hoping to save."
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方なんてものは、起きた出来事を効率よく片づけるだけの存在だ。
findings.governingReading: The quotation says a champion efficiently deals with already occurred events.
findings.explanation: The remembered cleanup criticism receives an additional never-save-the-people claim.

findings.highlight: This man has been consumed by the darkness.
findings.evidenceJa: 男は、黒い汚濁を飲み込んでいた。
findings.governingReading: Kirei has taken the black contamination into himself.
findings.explanation: The man swallowing corruption becomes corruption consuming him.

findings.highlight: His heart is ashen. He's draped in shadow.
findings.evidenceJa: 心臓は黒く、何か、得体の知れない闇に包まれている。
findings.governingReading: 黒い and 黒こげ specify black darkness and charred-black bodies.
findings.explanation: Black heart/charred bodies are rendered as ashen.

findings.highlight: "You may trust me. I have no wish to fight. Though the situation is dire, I will not refuse you your right to seek the Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 「信じたまえ。私はおまえたちと争う気はない。期せずしてこのような形になってしまったが、おまえたちが聖杯を獲ろうというのなら邪魔はしない。
findings.governingReading: Kirei calls the present arrangement unplanned/unexpected as part of his peaceable pose.
findings.explanation: The unintended situation becomes a dire situation.

findings.highlight: "It is. It exists in the ether.
findings.evidenceJa: 「有るとも。聖杯は何処にでもある。
findings.governingReading: He claims it can be anywhere.
findings.explanation: The Grail existing everywhere becomes existing in the ether.

findings.highlight: I thought it was supposed to manifest when there's only one Servant left. That a lie, then?"
findings.evidenceJa: アレは残り一人にならなければ現れない物じゃなかったのか。オレたちを呼んだ連中は、初めからペテンにかけてたって事か？」
findings.governingReading: Lancer asks whether those who called them had deceived them from the beginning.
findings.explanation: A lie question loses the accused summoners and original deception.

findings.highlight: Wouldn't you agree, Saber? You are a finalist from the previous war. You must have seen the truth. You know what kind of Grail manifests here."
findings.evidenceJa: そうであろうセイバー？　おまえとて前回最後まで残ったサーヴァントだ。アインツベルンの用意した“聖杯”がどんなものか、薄々判っているのではないか？」
findings.governingReading: Kirei asks if she vaguely understands the kind of Grail prepared by the Einzberns.
findings.explanation: Faint knowledge of the Einzbern-prepared Grail becomes seeing the truth and knowing the local manifestation.

findings.highlight: "I said I can make a selection. I will gladly hand over the Grail to the right person.
findings.evidenceJa: 「私は選定役だと言っただろう。相応しい人間がいるのならば、喜んで聖杯は譲る。
findings.governingReading: He repeats that his role is selecting the worthy owner.
findings.explanation: Claiming the selector role becomes claiming selection ability.

findings.highlight: The Holy Grail only responds to those who have a wish. Surely you must be curious as to whether your Master actually wants the Grail."
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯は求める者にのみ応える。己れのマスターが聖杯に相応しいかどうか、おまえとて興味はあろう」
findings.governingReading: Kirei says Saber must be interested in her Master’s fitness/worthiness for it.
findings.explanation: Whether the Master is worthy becomes whether he wants the Grail.

findings.highlight: Is he so free from sin that he does not curse that day ten years ago? Does he not tremble when he thinks of what it means for his future?"
findings.evidenceJa: 例えば、そう。十年前のあの日、この少年は本当に何も恨まなかったのか。その先にあったものを、忘れる事で振り払っているのではないか」
findings.governingReading: He asks whether the boy resented nothing that day and dispels what lies beyond it by forgetting.
findings.explanation: Resentment and forgetting buried aftermath become sinlessness and future fear.

findings.highlight: So many died that they had to hold mass funerals.
findings.evidenceJa: 大きな建物で、死んでしまった人たちの葬式が行われたからだ。
findings.governingReading: He saw grieving people as well as dying people; funerals held in a large building explain his encounter with the mourners.
findings.explanation: The source explains where Shirou saw the mourners. The English instead says the death toll required mass funerals, adding a logistical explanation the passage does not give.

findings.highlight: I kept moving forward, void of all reason.
findings.evidenceJa: 空っぽになった心で、それでも前に進まなければ許されないと。
findings.governingReading: With his inner self emptied out, he believed he would not be forgiven unless he nevertheless kept moving forward.
findings.explanation: An emptied inner life governed by “I must go on to be forgiven” becomes movement “void of all reason.” The English loses the specific obligation driving him.

findings.highlight: The kindness of neighbors.
findings.evidenceJa: 誰よりも優しかった誰か。
findings.governingReading: He recalls someone kinder than anyone.
findings.explanation: An unspecified supremely kind person becomes neighbors.

findings.highlight: I was no longer in pain.
findings.evidenceJa: それは辛いことじゃない。
findings.governingReading: それ refers to closing the earlier memories; he says that act is not painful and he was happy with Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: That memory closure was not painful becomes no longer in pain.

findings.highlight: Begging for death is no longer an option.
findings.evidenceJa: いっそ死にたいなんて思うものか。
findings.governingReading: He resolves not even to think he would rather be dead.
findings.explanation: Refusing to think I’d rather die becomes death-begging no longer an option.

findings.highlight: Do you not want that? Is that not your salvation?"
findings.evidenceJa: それこそが—おまえ自身を救う、唯一の方法ではないのかな」
findings.governingReading: Kirei offers this as the sole way to save Shirou himself.
findings.explanation: The only means of self-salvation becomes merely your salvation.

findings.highlight: No such miracle happened. Instead, I was left with this painful reality.
findings.evidenceJa: それも叶わず、現実を受け入れたけど。
findings.governingReading: The hoped-for awakening never came and he accepted reality.
findings.explanation: Accepting reality becomes being left with painful reality.

findings.highlight: It's the suffering that makes the goodness shine all the brighter.
findings.evidenceJa: 死は悲しく、同時に、輝かしいまでの思い出を残していく。
findings.governingReading: Death is sorrowful and also leaves radiant memories; pain is not its only legacy.
findings.explanation: Sorrow and radiant memories coexist in the Japanese. The English instead says suffering makes goodness brighter, changing the reasoning behind Shirou's defense of remembrance.

findings.highlight: Those deaths, they shaped me.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が彼らの死に縛られているように。
findings.governingReading: The deaths continue to bind him, while memories of Kiritsugu protect him.
findings.explanation: The deaths still influence Shirou, but being bound by them becomes being shaped by them. This weakens the contrast between their constraint and Kiritsugu's protective memory.

findings.highlight: And those memories form the path that eventually intertwines with others.
findings.evidenceJa: だから思い出は礎となって、今を生きている人間を変えていくのだと信じている。
findings.governingReading: He believes memories form a foundation and change people now alive.
findings.explanation: Memories transforming living people become paths intertwining with others.
